Lung, right upper lobe, lobectomy

The specimen consists of a right upper lobe lobectomy specimen (180 g, 150 x 110 x 45 mm). The visceral pleura is puckered over the tumour. Sectioning reveals a firm, tan-white, spiculated, anthracotic tumour measuring 23 mm in greatest dimension (23 x 20 x 18 mm), subpleural, 35 mm from the bronchial margin. The remaining lung parenchyma is spongy and unremarkable.

Microscopic findings
- Histologic type: Invasive adenocarcinoma, acinar predominant (acinar 60 %,
  papillary 25 %, solid 15 %)
- Histologic grade: Grade 2 (IASLC 2020; acinar predominant, 15 % high-grade
  patterns)
- Tumour histology:
  Sections show an invasive adenocarcinoma, acinar predominant (acinar 60 %,
  papillary 25 %, solid 15 %). The acinar areas consist of round to oval
  malignant glands set in fibrous stroma. The tumour cells are cuboidal to
  columnar with eosinophilic to vacuolated cytoplasm, enlarged nuclei showing
  vesicular chromatin and conspicuous nucleoli, and infiltrate a desmoplastic
  stroma. The tumour invades the visceral pleura (PL1, confirmed on elastic
  stain). Immunohistochemistry: TTF-1 positive, napsin A positive, p40 negative.
- Spread through air spaces (STAS): Not identified
- Visceral pleura invasion: PL1, extension through elastic membrane (elastic
